name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy has been actively releasing updates through mid-2026, with the latest being v2.26.3 (July 20, 2026), a hotfix adding an IP abuse ban-feed mechanism (ban-file, ban-window, ban-threshold, ban-weights) to help fail2ban block abusive IPs faster. v2.26.0 (July 9, 2026) patched a CPU denial-of-service vulnerability in message templates and added configurable date/time formats in the web app. v2.25.0 (June 24, 2026) introduced password reset via emailed magic links, reworked email verification to use durable single-use tokens, and switched to a cryptographically secure RNG for token generation. v2.24.0 (June 4, 2026) added an opt-in in-memory ACL cache and fixed a critical case-insensitive ACL topic-matching bug on SQLite. Full release notes are available at https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL (client); dual-licensed — check https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy for specifics
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in June–July 2026 with active bug fixes, security patches, and feature additions
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — supports ACL-based access control, account tokens, topic reservations, and an optional in-memory ACL cache (auth-access-cache)
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud instance

breaking_excerpts: Fix case-insensitive ACL topic matching on SQLite: an access control rule for 'secret' no longer also matches a request for 'SECRET' — this is a behavior change that may affect existing ACL rules on SQLite-backed servers.
Rework email verification to use durable, single-use, expiring magic links instead of in-memory 6-digit codes — existing in-flight verification codes will no longer work after upgrading.

Stop silently stripping spaces from passwords in web app login/signup/password-reset forms — users with passwords containing spaces who previously could not log in may now succeed, but behavior change could affect automated flows.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a versatile open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server with its own push infrastructure.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notifications and file sharing with polished apps but is a proprietary cloud service with a limited free tier and no self-hosting capability.

alternatives.name: Ntfy.sh (self-hosted via Synapse/Matrix)
alternatives.review: Matrix/Element offers federated, end-to-end encrypted messaging and notifications but is far more complex to operate and overkill for simple script-driven push notifications.
